doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Riverboat bands and Fate Marable in Cincinnati
summary: Daughtry asks about river bands; Russell recalls riverboat drummers staying at his house, one romancing his cousin, and bands moving from New Orleans to St. Louis to Cincinnati.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I want to say Ben Webster, but Ben wasn’t a big fat guy in those days. Big fat guy? It sounds like he should have been in Basie’s band. I’m blank right now. But a lot of people went through that school. You – it’s sort of setting the stage, but also going back. I’m seeing a kid who’s seeing the riverboat bands. Those bands used to have some good drummers. Who were some of the bands that – can you recall any of the bands that you used to see coming up the river there?
I used to know the name of the drummer, because I was only interested in the drummer.
Okay, see – was – what’s his name? He always – did he play a calliope?
It wasn’t Slim. It was . . .
I’m thinking of the bandleader, early ’20s, but I think he was still playing. Fate Marable. Was . . . ?
Fate Marable, yeah. That rings a bell.
He went for a long time. I think even Armstrong was with him for a very short period of time.
Really?

But those bands – we have to back up again. We have the railroad, and then the other dominant mode of transportation were the rivers. The Ohio River was like a main street. Then here you are living in – I think Cincinnati’s called the Queen City or something?
The Queen City.
Okay, and that has to do with being on the . . .

I remember that the drummer, who – he was really slick and really sharp, and I could understand him falling for my – what was she? – my – she wasn’t my sister, but my cousin. She came from the St. Louis family. He fell for her. They were at my house, the drummer and her. Fate Marable was – did he play drums?
You know what I’m thinking? He played some version of the piano and something called a calliope, which is some kind of organ? Is that . . . ?
That early he played?

I just remember him more as a bandleader who played for a long time, because when I was looking back at that era, I know he was playing in the late teens and he was still playing by the late ’20s and early ’30s. It was pretty much fading out then, the whole thing on the river, but he was like an institution. There were others, but that’s the one name that I remember.
I remember that they stayed at my house, some people in that band. We welcomed them. One of them went with Sara, my cousin.
Caught his eye, huh?
That’s what I loved about – I loved the way that they looked as much as the way they played.
You’re talking about people coming from somewhere else and bring a little bit of that with them. I’ll bet that was a lot of fun. Those were big times.
Absolutely. I believe they came up from New Orleans to St. Louis and then to Cincinnati and to Pittsburgh, and then back.
